variants.title: Franck-Hertz experiment with a mercury tube
variants.sample: Mercury vapour tube in a thermostatted oven
variants.unknown: the first excitation potential of mercury
variants.note: The classic tube of Franck and Hertz. The oven holds the mercury at about 180 degrees Celsius so that the vapour is thick enough for the dips to be deep.

source.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database: mercury 6s6p 3P1 level at 4.887 eV (the 253.7 nm resonance line)

variants.title: Franck-Hertz experiment with a neon tube
variants.unknown: the excitation potential of neon seen in this tube
variants.note: A neon tube needs no oven, and the layers of orange glow between the grid and the cathode can be seen with the eye. Its dips come about 18.7 V apart: not neon's lowest excited states at 16.6-16.9 eV, but the 2p levels at 18.4-19.0 eV, which the electrons excite far more readily.

source.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database: neon 2p5 3p levels at 18.38-18.97 eV, above the 2p5 3s levels at 16.62-16.85 eV

variants.title: Franck-Hertz experiment with an argon tube
variants.unknown: the first excitation potential of argon
variants.note: Argon's lowest excited states lie close together just above 11.5 eV, so the dips come about 11.6 V apart.

source.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database: argon 3p5 4s levels at 11.55-11.83 eV
